subject.title: Feature: Silence Watchdog + Response Delivery Confirmation — runtime-enforced operator visibility

question: Should OpenClaw add a default-on, channel-agnostic runtime policy for silence beacons plus response delivery confirmation/retry alerts, or keep the remaining work split across narrower heartbeat and durable-delivery issues?
rationale: The current code has adjacent foundations, but this issue asks for new default user-visible behavior, config, retries, and channel contract semantics that affect compatibility and operator expectations across channels.

options.title: Keep umbrella open and split implementation
options.body: Use this issue to coordinate policy while landing bounded watchdog and delivery-confirmation pieces through narrower issues such as https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/77771, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/87561, and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/46830.

options.title: Close after choosing canonical trackers
options.body: If maintainers want only narrower trackers, close this issue as superseded after explicitly naming which open issues own the silence-watchdog and delivery-confirmation halves.

options.title: Sponsor one combined core feature
options.body: Define the default config, retry/alert behavior, and cross-channel ACK contract here before implementation begins.

recommendation.title: Keep umbrella open and split implementation
recommendation.body: Use this issue to coordinate policy while landing bounded watchdog and delivery-confirmation pieces through narrower issues such as https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/77771, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/87561, and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/46830.

likelyOwner.reason: The maintainer-labeled durable final fallback issue covers the core channel-delivery contract most likely to constrain the response-confirmation policy.
